title: Jest tests, debugging, deployment, and troubleshooting
objectives: Write local Jest tests in __tests__ that never deploy to Salesforce, using sfdx-lwc-jest wire mocks.
Debug LWC with debug mode and Chrome DevTools, including wired data/error and LWS differences.
Treat LWC source as metadata you deploy; treat Jest as local-only artifacts listed in .forceignore.
Troubleshoot wires, tests, and production issues without confusing Jest with Lightning Testing Service.
diagnostic_question: A Jest test passes locally, the LWC fails on the record page, and debug logs show nothing. How do you split Jest tests, debugging, deployment, and troubleshooting?
definition: Jest tests for LWC are local JavaScript tests run with sfdx-lwc-jest. They live in a __tests__ folder, are committed to Git, and are never saved to Salesforce (.forceignore). Debugging uses Lightning debug mode and Chrome DevTools, with extra notes when Lightning Web Security is on. Deployment pushes the component metadata, not the tests. Troubleshooting follows wire payloads, config completeness, and test mocks that must not depend on live org data. ([Write Jest Tests](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/unit-testing-using-jest-create-tests.html); [Write Jest Tests for Wire Service](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/unit-testing-using-wire-utility.html); [Debug Wire Adapters](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/debug-wire.html))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who say Jest runs in the org, who mock nothing and hit Salesforce from CI, or who debug minified production JS. Jest is not Lightning Testing Service (Jasmine/Mocha). A green test that never connected the element to the DOM is a false pass.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an aircraft hangar. Jest is a pre-flight checklist on a mock fuselage—you control the weather. Debugging is the flight-data recorder and a well-lit hangar (debug mode). Deployment is releasing the real aircraft to the gate; the checklist binder stays on the ground. Troubleshooting is finding why the engine light is on: missing fuel ($recordId), bad mock weather, or a production-only LWS distortion.
deeper_explanation: Create tests with sf force lightning lwc test create, or add __tests__/component.test.js yourself. Jest runs local .js files ending in .test.js (recommended). Add **/__tests__/** to .forceignore so push/pull never sends tests to Salesforce. Jest is not Lightning Testing Service. ([Write Jest Tests](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/unit-testing-using-jest-create-tests.html))

Wire tests must not depend on org latency. sfdx-lwc-jest provides generic, LDS, and Apex wire adapters. Import the same adapter as production code, emit mock JSON, append the element to the DOM (wires provision only when connected), then Promise.resolve() before asserting. Prefer UI API snapshots over hand-written JSON. Spring ’21 registration APIs still work but are not recommended. ([Wire Jest utility](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/unit-testing-using-wire-utility.html))

Debug: enable debug mode for unminified JS. For wires, inspect data/error in Sources or use custom formatters ($0 on the element). An undefined $ param means both data and error stay undefined. With LWS, enable debug mode first; some debugging differences exist versus non-LWS. ([Debug Wire Adapters](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/debug-wire.html); [Debug with LWS Enabled](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/debug-lwsec.html))

Jest debug: Salesforce Extension Pack LWC Tests sidebar, or npm run test:unit:debug which runs sfdx-lwc-jest --debug, then chrome://inspect. Chrome does not honor VS Code breakpoints unless you use debugger statements in that flow. ([Debug Jest Tests](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/unit-testing-using-jest-debug-tests.html))
Deployment is metadata (the LWC bundle minus tests). Troubleshooting production: confirm the bundle deployed, FLS, wire config, LWS/CSP (LWC-010), and that you are not chasing a Jest-only mock.

mental_model.analogy: An aircraft hangar: mock fuselage checklist (Jest), flight recorder in a lit hangar (debug mode), release to the gate (deploy metadata), engine-light diagnosis (troubleshooting).
useful_mapping: mock fuselage → Jest with emit() data, no live org
checklist binder stays on the ground → __tests__ in .forceignore
well-lit hangar → debug mode unminified JS
release to the gate → deploy LWC metadata
engine light → undefined $recordId, LWS distortion, or missed DOM connect in the test
old Jasmine trolley → Lightning Testing Service, not Jest
where_it_breaks: A real pre-flight still uses real fuel; Jest must not call Salesforce.
Green Jest does not prove FLS or LWS in the org.
chrome://inspect ignores VS Code breakpoints unless you use debugger.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Jest is local and git-tracked, never in the org. I mock wires with emit after DOM connect. I debug in the org with debug mode. I deploy metadata, then troubleshoot $ params, LWS, and FLS separately from CI green.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I contrast Jest with LTS. I show __tests__ and .forceignore. I refuse tests that call Salesforce. If production fails, I turn on debug mode, inspect the wired object, and check LWS. A test that never appended the element is invalid.

terminology.plain: Local unit tests for an LWC that run on your machine or CI, not in Salesforce.
terminology.precise: sfdx-lwc-jest, files under __tests__, recommended *.test.js. Input must be fully controlled; mock wires.
terminology.example: labOpenCases.test.js emitting a mock related-list payload.
terminology.non_example: Apex @IsTest class, or LTS Jasmine in the org.
terminology.boundary: End-to-end UI tests are a different Guide section.

terminology.plain: The Salesforce Jest runner and wire-mock utility for LWC.
terminology.precise: Generic, LDS, and Apex wire adapters with emit(). Prefer this over wiring @salesforce/wire-service-jest-util alone.
terminology.non_example: Live REST calls to UI API from the test.
terminology.boundary: Adapter internals are in the utility docs.

terminology.plain: Inspecting running LWC JavaScript in the browser or Jest inspector.
terminology.precise: Org: debug mode + Chrome, custom formatters for wires. Jest: inspect-brk / chrome://inspect. LWS orgs: debug mode first.
terminology.example: $0 on a c-lab-open-cases element to see wired config/data.
terminology.non_example: Reading only Apex debug logs for a template bug.
terminology.boundary: LWS-specific limits are on the security debug page.

terminology.plain: Sending the LWC bundle metadata to an org.
terminology.precise: JS/HTML/CSS/js-meta.xml deploy. Tests stay local via .forceignore. Green Jest does not mean the bundle is in production.
terminology.example: sf project deploy start of labOpenCases without __tests__.
terminology.non_example: Expecting Jest coverage to appear in Apex coverage.

terminology.plain: Finding why the component misbehaves in tests or in the org.
terminology.precise: Split Jest-only failures (mocks, DOM) from org-only (FLS, LWS, missing deploy, undefined $ params).
terminology.example: data and error still undefined because recordId never set.
terminology.non_example: Rewriting SLDS first (LWC-009) for a wire that never fired.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Performance freeze (LWC-011) versus a thrown error.
terminology.boundary: Start from payload and config, not random Setup clicks.

terminology.precise: Must include **/__tests__/** so Jest never becomes org metadata.
terminology.example: sf force lightning lwc test setup adds the glob.

when_to_use: When you must prove LWC behavior with Jest tests, then debug, deploy, and troubleshoot the org copy separately.
When a wire test should emit mock JSON instead of calling Salesforce.
When production JS is minified: enable debug mode before Chrome stepping, especially with LWS.
When someone expects Jest files to appear in the org: explain .forceignore and metadata deployment.
when_not_to_use: Do not use Jest as a substitute for Apex tests, FLS verification, or LWS org testing.
Do not treat Lightning Testing Service Jasmine tests as sfdx-lwc-jest, or deploy __tests__ to Salesforce.
Do not debug minified production LWC without debug mode, or honor only VS Code breakpoints in chrome://inspect.
Do not call a test valid if the element was never connected to the DOM before emit.

decision_table.not: A live UI API call from the test, or an Apex @IsTest for the HTML.

decision_table.signal: Need to step through minified Lightning JS.

interview_questions.question: How do Jest tests, debugging, deployment, and troubleshooting split for LWC?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Jest is local mocks in Git. Debugging is debug mode in the org. Deployment is metadata without tests. Troubleshooting decides which of those three is failing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I never say Jest runs on the server. I show __tests__ and .forceignore. I mock wires with emit after connect. If the page fails, I inspect $ params and LWS, not the mock. I do not equate Jest coverage with Apex coverage.
interview_questions.example: labProductCard: CI green, page blank until recordId is passed.
follow_ups: How do you mock Apex wires?

interview_questions.question: Walk through a correct Jest test for a wired getRecord.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Import the same adapter, load JSON, create and append the element, emit, Promise.resolve, assert shadow DOM text.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I stress connect-before-emit. I prefer a UI API snapshot. I name generic versus LDS versus Apex adapters. I do not hit Salesforce from CI. Spring ’21 register calls are legacy.
tradeoffs: One file versus many test files
follow_ups: How do you test the error path?
weak_answer_warnings: fetch() the record in the test

interview_questions.question: Jest passed, production users see a blank card. Your first hour?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Confirm deploy, enable debug mode, inspect wire config. Look for undefined recordId, FLS, or LWS. Do not delete mocks.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat green Jest as proof of rendering logic given a fixture. The org supplies identity and access. I check js-meta.xml targets and whether the page actually assigns the Id. I compare LWS between scratch and prod if a library is involved.
interview_questions.example: Quick action vs record page recordId timing from LWC-008 combined with this lesson.
tradeoffs: More integration tests versus faster unit tests
follow_ups: Would an E2E test have caught it?
weak_answer_warnings: Jest is wrong because production failed

interview_questions.question: A teammate commits real Account JSON from production into __tests__/data. What do you do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Remove it. That is data exposure. Replace with a synthetic UI API-shaped fixture using LAB_ names.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The Guide wants realistic shape, not real PII. I rotate anything that leaked, add a review check, and keep snapshots from a sandbox. This is LWC-010 meeting LWC-012.
interview_questions.example: Replacing a production getRecord dump with a sandbox snapshot of a LAB_ Account.

interview_questions.question: Your wire test never updates the DOM. Checklist?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Connected? Same adapter import? emit after append? Promise.resolve? Mock shape match?
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I also check they used the LDS adapter when the component uses uiRecordApi. I look for querying the wrong CSS class. I do not start with LWS; Jest is not the org sandbox.
tradeoffs: One fat test versus focused cases
follow_ups: How do you emit an error?

interview_questions.question: How do you debug a wired property on a live page?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Debug mode, custom formatters, select the element, inspect data, error, config, isDataProvisionedForConfig.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If both data and error are undefined, I look at config completeness. I do not wrap @wire in try-catch (LWC-007). With LWS I still start with debug mode. Apex logs will not show a missing $ param.
tradeoffs: Wired property versus wired function for debug
follow_ups: What is context on the formatter?

interview_questions.question: When are Jest tests not enough to ship?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the risk is FLS, LWS, CSP, container support, or data volume. Those need org or performance tests.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still require Jest for rendering branches (loading/empty/error). I add Apex tests for the server. I do a sandbox keyboard/mobile pass (LWC-009) and a payload review (LWC-010/011). Jest is necessary and not sufficient.
interview_questions.example: Shipping labCaseGrid with Jest but 3,000 rows in UAT—still a fail.

interview_questions.question: Teach this with a hangar analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Jest is a mock fuselage checklist. Debug mode is a lit hangar. Deploy sends the plane, not the binder. The break: real flights still need real fuel—recordId and FLS—that mocks cannot supply.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I also break Chrome inspect versus VS Code breakpoints. I mention LTS as the old trolley. I never use a library metaphor. Troubleshooting is reading the engine light: missing $ param versus distortion versus failed deploy.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard Git → Jest vs Git → deploy arrows, no arrow from Jest to the org.
